liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): The Scarlet Begonias introduction is praised as exactly what one wants from a kind Scarlet; Scarlet into Fire is called hot, and Big Railroad Blues in the middle is liked [13][16][22]
- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Jack Straw alone makes the show worth having, according to this reviewer; Jack Straw is said to smoke here, and the Althea before it is also great [14][21]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Scarlet into Fire shows classic band interplay and a beautifully measured transition into Fire; Jerry snakes into Fire with the drums guiding the transition; described as sultry [17][19]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer rates the Estimated Prophet into Eyes of the World sequence extremely highly, along with Big Railroad Blues [13]
- **Althea** (1 review): Althea and Jack Straw are called among the best versions ever, with Jerry playing strongly [15]
- **The // Promised Land** (1 review): Reviewer calls this one of the best Promised Lands ever [16]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Black Peter, Althea, Jack Straw and Estimated into Eyes are recommended highlights, plus the acoustic set [22]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer notes a hot Franklin's Tower [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd80-10-10 s1t01 On The Road Again**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t02 It Must Have Been The Roses**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t03 Monkey & The Engineer**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t04 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t05 Dark Hollow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t06 To Lay Me Down**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t07 Heaven Help The Fool**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd80-10-10 s1t08 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-10.144766.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 35 songs; 228 min [1]
- **gd1980-10-10.mtx.chappell.sb03.28740.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 224 min; rated 4.33/5 by 15 [3]
- **gd80-10-10.menke.vernon.13989.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 32 songs; 223 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is nice and conveys the feel of the room [19]
- **gd1980-10-10.156341.akg-se5-wiseman-miller-clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 32 songs; 220 min [5]
- **gd80-10-10.sbd.cousinit.24710.sbefail.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4.18/5 by 11 [8]. Said about its sound: Matrix starts with a decent audience-heavy section near New Minglewood Blues, then switches to a better-quality soundboard portion; Reviewer finds the matrix a less than crisp board recording rather than an audience tape [16][23]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this show introduced many people to the Dead while at boarding school [14]
- Reviewer's boarding school had a soundboard copy of this show around 1981 [15]
- Space into Truckin' is included within the Truckin' track [1]
- Reviewer attended all the weekend shows at this venue and considers the acoustic set on the 11th the best [12]
- Reviewer says the 11/30/80 Fox show has a far better Scarlet>Fire than this one [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-10.144766.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5(Maxell UDXLI) [1]
- **gd1980-10-10.mtx.chappell.sb03.28740.flac16**: transferred by Chris Chappell [3]. Also: Nakamichi CM700 mics through a mixer to Sony D-5; first-generation cassette remastered with pitch correction by Douglas Ferguson [3]
- **gd80-10-10.menke.vernon.13989.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bob Menke; source: Audience Recording: Nakamichi CM700's [4]. Also: Bob Menke taped from the balcony with three Nakamichi CM700 mics through a mixer to a Sony D-5 [4]
- **gd1980-10-10.156341.akg-se5-wiseman-miller-clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [5]. Also: Scott Wiseman supplied the AKG source cassettes and transfer; Ron Ellner's Nakamichi 700 source fills several gaps [5]
- **gd80-10-10.sbd.cousinit.24710.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Bob Menke; source: Audience Recording: Nakamichi CM700's [8]
